'''''Gladiolus italicus''''' is a species of [[gladiolus]] known by the common names '''Italian gladiolus''', '''field gladiolus''', and '''common sword-lily'''.
It is native to much of Eurasia and North Africa,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=328527|title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|website=wcsp.science.kew.org}}</ref> but it is well known on other continents where it is a common [[noxious weed|weed]], particularly of cultivated fields and waste places.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=240010021|title=Gladiolus italicus in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org}}</ref> This perennial flower grows an erect stem approaching a meter in maximum height with a few long leaves around its base. Toward the top half of the generally unbranching stem is a spike [[inflorescence]] on which flowers appear at intervals. Each plant has up to 15 or 16 flowers. The flower is bright pink to magenta and several centimeters long with its [[stamen]]s and [[Gynoecium|style]] protruding from the throat. The fruit is a capsule about a centimeter long containing many seeds.<ref>Meikle, R.D. (1985). Flora of Cyprus 2: 833-1970. The Bentham-Moxon Trust Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref><ref>Boulos, L.
